questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why modern life is stressful and how to manage it
How to pass important exams without studying
Why young people work too many hours a week
The health benefits of listening to music daily
questions.why: They discuss what makes us stressed and how to manage stress to feel happier and healthier.

options: Taking important exams
Watching the news every evening
Not having enough time to do something
Meeting lots of new people at parties
questions.why: Neil says not having enough time to do something really makes him stressed out.

questions.q: What makes Becca feel stressed, and how does Neil respond?
options: Being late for work; Neil says he never is
Working alone at home; Neil prefers it
Loud noise at night; Neil doesn't mind it
Trying new things she's bad at; Neil agrees
questions.why: Becca is stressed trying something new she isn't good at, and Neil says 'I find that stressful, too.'

questions.q: How does Neil cope with stressful situations?
options: He goes for a long run in the park to relax
He slows down, breathes and says it'll be OK
He makes a detailed to-do list for the day
He calls his friends and talks about it
questions.why: He tries to slow down, pause, take a breath and think everything will be OK again later.

questions.q: According to Claudia Hammond, what can happen if overwhelm continues for a long time?
options: It can lead to burnout
It always goes away by itself
It makes people work faster
It improves memory
questions.why: She says if it becomes chronic stress, 'that might lead to burnout in the end'.

questions.q: What does Claudia say about feeling stressed during an exam?
options: You should leave the exam room and take a break
It always makes your final results much worse
You should try hard not to think about it at all
It may help you think clearly and do better
questions.why: She says you may well perform better while stressed, as nerves sharpen your thinking.

questions.q: Which of these is another tip from Claudia for reducing stress?
options: Always aim for perfection
Accept that being 'good enough' is fine
Work faster to finish everything
Avoid all difficult tasks
questions.why: Neil says her tips include slowing down and accepting it's OK to be 'good enough'.

questions.q: Why does Claudia say we should accept that our to-do list will never end?
options: Because to-do lists are a complete waste of time
Because we should all do much less work
Because a list that never ends is just normal life
Because other people should do some of our tasks
questions.why: She says there will always be something new on it, 'and that's just life'.
